residual_risks: Replacing a loaded Windows executable changes the next launch; the current process continues using its retained image. Activation and rollback therefore require verification after a normal restart, without terminating a user session.
Rollback intentionally refuses foreign edits and tampered backups. Preserve the manifest, byte backups and journal-owned retained images until recovery and post-restart verification are complete.
The migration journal supports process interruption, but its writes are not explicitly fsync-backed; sudden power loss durability was not established by the inspected interruption tests.
testing_gaps: Final source-to-built-artifact hashes, NSIS bundle inspection, actual installation and post-restart runtime evidence remain pending with the parent release workflow. These are release evidence gates, not asserted code defects.

deployment_notes.status: Code review found no additional concrete deployment defects; release acceptance remains conditional on the pending build and installation evidence.
reviewed: build-native.ps1 builds both locked Cargo manifests, copies the helper and Node addon, then hashes their bytes into native/manifest.json using native-hash.ps1.
run-release-build.ps1 records native Tauri exit status in target/release-build-result.json; ensure the root target directory exists before launching this wrapper.
Tauri resources include desktop/native and native, and desktop package/config versions both read 0.2.5. verify-desktop-binary.ps1 validates ProductVersion and outputs SHA256.

deploy-performance.py checks native and Advisor payload hashes, guards the verified kernel and Advisor version, validates destination containment, backs up previous bytes and installs the desktop executable last.
The Advisor deployment manifest names exactly index.js, observer.js and turn-tracker.js; the rejected side-panel experiment is excluded.

Install and rollback image-rename intent is journaled before rename. Recovery validates the expected sibling name, roots and SHA256 before restoring. The nine reported passing deployment tests were inspected, not rerun.
checklist: Record the exact reviewed source revision and working-tree state, require release-build-result.json exitCode=0, and preserve full build output.
Verify the executable ProductVersion is 0.2.5 and record its SHA256; match bundled native payload hashes to native/manifest.json and verify expected adapter resources exist in the bundle.
Run deploy-performance.py without --apply and preserve its concrete target list before the authorized installation step.
After apply, require manifest status=applied and verify each target against afterSha256; preserve the rollback directory.
After a normal desktop restart, confirm the actual executable path/version, native persistence activation, session search behavior and helper disposal using the parent runtime checks.
Verify native-disabled and unsupported-kernel paths retain official session access. Compare original session data/config using the parent baseline evidence.
Review native cache integrity using the queries in data-migrations.json when needed; never run migration or cleanup against authoritative logs.
rollback: Require manifest status=rolled-back and confirm all restored targets equal beforeSha256, with originally absent files absent.
If interruption occurs, rerun rollback with the same manifest. Do not remove retained images or alter journal entries to bypass ownership/hash failures.

A currently loaded newly installed addon or executable may keep its running process on the new implementation until normal exit. Verify restored behavior only after normal restart; do not stop the user's process as part of this review.
Cache schema rollback is unnecessary for official operation because the cache is disposable and original logs are not rewritten.
